children: The increase of agentic AI use cases is leading to a surge in CPU demand, which is expected to drive up CPU shipments and benefit CPU servers and memory makers, according to Mizuho.

"We estimate agentic CPUs reaching ~$80B by 2030E (~123% 4Y CAGR), head-node CPUs to $68B (~61% 4Y CAGR), and traditional CPUs to $60B (~2% 4Y CAGR)," said Mizuho analysts, led by Vijay Rakesh, in an investor report. "Total Server CPU TAM we estimate reaches ~$209B by 2030E (32% 4Y CAGR) and is conservatively below AMD's

target of >$220B. Our bottom-up projection sees Agentic AI driving CPU, DRAM, and NAND growing to 22-30% of their respective total markets (number of bits shipped). Our model estimates Agentic AI CPU demand as a % of total server CPUs grows from ~4% today to ~30% by 2030E."
The estimated demand gains prompted Mizuho to increase its price target on AMD to $705 from $580, Dell
to $650 from $600, Intel
to $114 from $92, Sandisk
to $2,050 from $1,875 and SMCI
to $43 from $35. Mizuho maintains an Outperform rating on all the above, except for SMCI, which is rated Neutral.
Mizuho pointed to the recent popularity of Meta's
Muse, a personal AI agent, and the release of OpenAI's
Dots as evidence of deeper integration of agents into daily work processes.
In the near term, Mizuho identifies four leading-edge CPUs for agentic workloads. This includes Arm's
AGI CPU, AMD's Venice, Nvidia's
Vera and Intel's
Diamond Rapids.
Mizuho maintained its $325 price target and Outperform rating on Nvidia.

"We see server CPU revenues rapidly expanding, driven mainly by Agentic AI, as we note NVDA ramping well and ARM entering the fray with its first HW product," Rakesh noted. "We see AMD and INTC both growing steadily from ~$12B/$17B in 2025 to ~$44B/$41B by 2028E, while NVDA we believe sees the steepest ramp, scaling from ~$7B to ~$60B, overtaking peers by 2027E as Vera ramps merchant CPU share with the introduction of its first Vera-only racks containing 72 GPUs alongside its GPU attach head nodes."

"Separately, we believe DELL and SMCI's CPU- only server revenue could continue to drive upside into 2027E and beyond, with DELL scaling from ~$19B in 2025 to ~$40B by 2028E, while SMCI potentially grows from $7B in 2025 to $17B fueled by Agentic AI orchestration demand, alongside traditional enterprise server deployments," he added.
Mizuho also reiterated its Outperform rating and $1,400 target on Micron

title: Agentic AI drives up CPU demand; Mizuho ups targets on AMD, Intel
